trial_court_outcome: Guilty verdict and sentenced both accused accordingly
high_court_outcome: Acquitted co-accused, upheld conviction of appellant
neutral_facts: The accused and a co-accused assaulted the victim with an axe and stick while the victim was returning from the market to his village. The victim died on the spot. The FIR was lodged by the victim's father, who stated that the accused had a land dispute with the victim and that the victim was previously charged with the murder of the accused's brother. The prosecution examined seven witnesses, including the victim's father and an eyewitness. The trial court convicted both accused under Sections 302 and 34 of the IPC. The High Court acquitted the co-accused based on the testimony of an eyewitness who could only identify the appellant. The Supreme Court overturned the High Court's decision, finding flaws in the prosecution's evidence, including the absence of a chemical analyst report, inconsistencies in the Test Identification Parade, and the unreliability of the eyewitness due to poor eyesight and unnatural conduct.
